parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
In a molecule of $\text{SOCl}_2$ the sulfur atom has four bonds.

Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram of $\text{SOCl}_2$. Show the outer shell electrons only.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
When $\text{SOCl}_2$ is reacted with a carboxylic acid to produce an acyl chloride, two acidic gases are formed.

$$\text{SOCl}_2\text{(l)} + \text{RCO}_2\text{H}\text{(l)} \rightarrow \text{RCOCl}\text{(l)} + \text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{HCl}\text{(g)}$$

A $1.00\text{ g}$ sample of a carboxylic acid $\text{RCO}_2\text{H}$ was treated in this way, and the gases were absorbed in $60.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NaOH}\text{(aq)}$, an excess.

parts.text: Write equations for the reactions between

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The excess $\text{NaOH}$ was titrated with $0.500\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{H}^+\text{(aq)}$. It required $10.8\text{ cm}^3$ of the $\text{H}^+\text{(aq)}$ solution to reach the end-point.

Calculate the total number of moles of $\text{NaOH}$ that reacted with the $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of $\text{RCO}_2\text{H}$ that produced the $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Hence calculate the $M_{\text{r}}$ of the carboxylic acid, $\text{RCO}_2\text{H}$.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
The R group contains carbon and hydrogen only.

Suggest the molecular formula of $\text{RCO}_2\text{H}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
The following synthetic route shows how a carboxylic acid can be converted into an amine.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} \xrightarrow{\text{SOCl}_2} \text{CH}_3\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_3} \text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{step 3}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Angelic acid, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, is a natural product isolated from the roots of the angelica plant.

- Angelic acid reacts with $\text{H}_2 + \text{Ni}$ to form $\mathbf{T}$, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$.
- $\mathbf{T}$ undergoes the above synthetic route to form the amine $\mathbf{U}$, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{13}\text{N}$.
- $\mathbf{U}$ can also be made by reacting 1-bromo-2-methylbutane with ammonia.

Both angelic acid and $\mathbf{T}$ exist as stereoisomers.

Suggest structures for angelic acid, $\mathbf{T}$ and $\mathbf{U}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: State the type of stereoisomerism shown by angelic acid and $\mathbf{T}$.
